title: High-loading <mark>all-solid-state</mark> lithium–sulfur batteries enabled by tailored sulfur–sulfide and sulfur–carbon interfaces
abstract: Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02813-1 <mark>All-solid-state</mark> lithium–sulfur batteries are a next-generation high-energy-density solution for energy storage. Here catholyte/cathode interfaces are found to be as important as transport tortuosity in thick sulfur cathodes, and an areal capacity of 10 mAh cm−2 is demonstrated at a <mark>stack pressure</mark> of 15 MPa and sulfur loading of 6.1 mg cm−2.

title: Li2TiO3 Powder Effects on LiCoO2 Electrode Reactions in <mark>Lithium</mark> Secondary Batteries
authors: Masaki Ogawa, Yoshinori Arachi and Tatsuya Nakamura
abstract: The <mark>specific capacity</mark> of a LiCoO2 positive electrode containing 10 wt% Li2TiO3 powder (LCO-10LT) exceeded that of a LiCoO2 electrode (LCO) alone at current densities up to around 6.0 mA cm−2. Findings indicate that Li2TiO3 activated the electrode reaction of the LiCoO2 electrode. The <mark>electrochemical impedance</mark> spectroscopy (EIS) using a symmetrical cell of 30 wt% Li2TiO3 powder (LCO-30LT) showed a marked decrease in resistance corresponding to a charge transfer at the electrode/electrolyte interface.
